cards.text: This is the word of the LORD that came to Hosea, a prophet (Hosea 1:1), and it brings a charge. Two kingdoms come up in it: Ephraim, the northern kingdom of Israel, and Judah, the southern kingdom. Get comfortable, friend, because this one's a full report.

cards.question: The first line of the charge says Ephraim surrounds Me with ___, the house of Israel with deceit.

cards.text: Then the prophecy turns to Judah, and that part opens with "but".

cards.question: The prophecy says Judah still walks with God and is faithful to the Holy One.

cards.text: Back to Ephraim: he feeds on the wind and chases the east wind all day long. That's me chasing one loose sprinkle with the oven fan running, and friend, that sprinkle is NOT coming back.

cards.question: Ephraim multiplies lies and violence, and he makes a covenant with Assyria, a powerful empire. What does he send to Egypt?

cards.text: Then the prophecy says the LORD has a charge to bring against Judah. It names Jacob too, Isaac's son and the forefather of Israel.

cards.question: The LORD will punish Jacob no matter what his ways and deeds have been.

cards.text: He will punish Jacob according to his ways and repay him according to his deeds. Then the prophecy goes all the way back to Jacob before he was even born.

cards.question: Jacob's grabbing starts early. Even in the womb, he grasped his brother's ___.

cards.text: When Jacob is grown and strong, he wrestles with God. Yes, he struggles with the angel and prevails, but that's not where it ends.

cards.question: Jacob struggles with the angel and prevails. What else does Jacob do?

answers.text: He weeps and seeks God's favor
He walks off without a word
He laughs and boasts of his win

cards.text: Jacob found Him at Bethel, a town in Canaan, and spoke with Him there: "the LORD God of Hosts, the LORD is His name of renown."
Then the prophecy stops telling Jacob's story and gives a call.

cards.question: After Jacob's story, the prophecy says, "But you must…" What must you do?
The call says to maintain love and justice, and to wait on your God only when times get hard.

cards.text: Then the prophecy points at a merchant who loves to cheat with dishonest scales in his hands. That's the guy selling a box marked a dozen with TEN cookies inside.

cards.question: Next, Ephraim boasts about how rich he has become.
Ephraim also claims something about himself in all his labors. What is it?

answers.text: No one can find sinful iniquity in him
He has worked harder than his brothers
He has given all his wealth away

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks: "But I am the LORD your God ever since the land of Egypt."

cards.question: The LORD tells the ones He's speaking to that He will again make them dwell in ___, as in the days of the appointed feast.

cards.text: Then the LORD says He has spoken. He multiplied visions and gave parables.

cards.question: The LORD says He gave those visions and parables through the kings.

cards.text: Then the prophecy calls out Gilead, a region east of the Jordan River, and Gilgal, a town in Israel. It asks if there's iniquity in Gilead and says they will surely come to nothing, and friend, that line has me checking my own counter for crumbs.

cards.question: The prophecy asks if they sacrifice bulls in Gilgal. What will their altars become?

answers.text: Heaps of stones in the field

cards.text: Then the prophecy brings up Jacob one more time. Jacob flees to the land of Aram, and friend, I couldn't flee anywhere if I tried, because every getaway I make is a HOP with a gold base attached.

cards.question: In Aram, Jacob, also called Israel (Genesis 32:28), tends sheep. He is working for a ___.
Jacob tended sheep for a wife. But by a ___ the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt.

cards.text: By a prophet, Israel was preserved too. Then the last line of the charge comes back around to Ephraim, and friend, set the dough down for this one.

cards.question: Ephraim has provoked bitter anger. What will his Lord leave upon him?

cards.text: And his Lord will repay him for his contempt. That's the charge, friend, laid out start to finish.
